reflection.text:
Post-unblinding review - demecolcine / colcemid - Verdict CORRECT (Microtubule destabilizers, p=0.87) - Truth: Microtubule destabilizers.

What got it right:

1. Quantitative nuclear morphology was the driver, not the visual call. Well w_fe26c7e5aa (10 uM, e2) and w_39e357ace8 (1 uM, e3) gave extreme solidity/form factor defects: nuc_solidity z=-48.7/-36.7, nuc_form_factor z=-45.3/-46.1, frac_large_nucleus z=+19.4. This was reproduced at w_4134b8c5f2 (0.1 uM) and w_17353b8062 (0.03 uM) with nuc_solidity z=-62.8/-69.9 and nuc_form_factor z=-51.5/-49.9 (e10, e11). The magnitude and persistence down to 0.03 uM argued for a potent mitotic-failure agent, not a high-dose off-target effect. Actin channels (act_std z=+25.1, +23.8, act_tub_ratio z=+17.9) were elevated but secondary to the nuclear lobulation, not primary actin disruption.

2. Atlas comparison compensated for lack of annotation. e19/e20 lookup_compound showed demecolcine has none curated in ChEMBL and PubChem CID 220401 alone gives no MoA, so we had to rely on phenotype. compare_to_reference_atlas at 2 wells was 2/2 NSC Microtubule destabilizers, k-neighbour 7/10 destabilizers / 3/10 Protein synthesis (e5), and after expanding to 4 wells across 0.03-10 uM it became unanimous 4/4 NSC (e12) with identical k-neighbour distribution. That convergence across dose justified hypothesis_history step 17 weighting Microtubule destabilizers 0.87 vs Aurora 0.07, citing e2,e3,e5,e10,e11,e12,e13.

3. Dose trend locked the large-nucleus phenotype. Early dose_response attempts (e6-e9) correctly failed - 'Need at least 3 wells over 2 concentrations' - which forced acquisition of the lower doses. With 4 wells, frac_large_nucleus rho=+1.00 p=0 (e13) provided monotonicity that Aurora alone would not predict as cleanly across this range, while frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=+0.60 p=0.4 (e14), act_mean rho=-0.40 (e15) and nuc_dna_integrated rho=-0.60 (e16) were non-significant and correctly not used to support a DNA-damage/replication story.

What misled / what I missed and why:

The sole contradicting evidence was e4 describe_phenotype: microscopist on 4 fields, density lower vs DMSO, 8 observations, candidates: Aurora kinase inhibitors. This is understandable - both Aurora inhibition and destabilizer-driven mitotic failure produce grape-cluster/lobulated nuclei and multinucleation by cytokinesis failure, and the microscopist admitted tubulin texture as uncharacterised on composites. I did not over-weight it because NSC consensus already outweighed visual similarity, but review critique is correct: I left the tubulin signature unstated. I acquired high/mid/low wells well to cover 0.03-10 uM but did not quantify tub_mean/tubulin texture dose response beyond the failed e9 attempt, and never ran a biochemical tubulin polymerization or phospho-histone H3 mitotic index comparison.

That gap matters for demecolcine, which is colcemid, a colchicine-site destabilizer. Phenotype alone cannot prove binding site; chemical-genetic corroboration is the lock. PMID 17938271 directly shows amino acid substitutions at proline 220 of beta-tubulin confer resistance to paclitaxel and colcemid, supporting colcemid as a tubulin-targeting destabilizer, and the broader tubulin-resistance literature e.g. PMID 22669706 on beta-tubulin mutations conferring paclitaxel resistance reinforces that genetic resistance mapping is the orthogonal test I proposed but did not execute in-run. My literature searches after unblinding (e21: 12 hits/5 returned for demecolcine/colchicine; e22: 0 hits for multinucleation phenotype) were not integrated into the blinded decision and would not have replaced an assay.

Calibration was appropriate: 0.87 left hedging for Aurora 0.07 and Protein synthesis 0.02 rather than 0.99, reflecting the review's point about non-specific morphology. Next time, I would acquire replicate wells earlier to power dose_response for frac_mitotic_like/cell_count/tub_mean from the start, and pair NSC vote with an orthogonal tubulin assay as noted in conclusions: tubulin polymerization + pH3/alpha-tubulin spindle morphology time course vs reference destabilizer and reference Aurora inhibitor to distinguish destabilizer-induced mitotic failure from Aurora cytokinesis failure.

No clinical implications discussed - this is screening data only.
